hook.text: A dead man's switch is useless if the transaction never lands. LegacyKeeper treats acceptance as the start, not the result.

problem.text: Most agents stop at an API response. LegacyKeeper requires settlement, a successful receipt, the expected event, and confirmed product state.

positioning.text: The owner signs one short-lived message. KeeperHub sponsors the transaction on Sepolia. LegacyKeeper then verifies the chain independently before showing success.

product.text: This is the live dashboard. It reads the deployed estate, the exact beneficiary split, and every retained execution attempt from real evidence.

heartbeat.text: A normal check-in never calls the contract directly. The browser sends only nonce, deadline, and signature to the workflow-specific KeeperHub webhook.

recovery.text: Failed attempts stay visible beside the recovered transaction. A separate x402 call also checked the live token allowance and changed the coverage verdict.

close.text: Five enabled workflows. Four automatic trigger types. One hundred and two passing tests. LegacyKeeper proves the last mile before it claims success.
